architecture_principles: the unit of decision is an experiment, not a formulation
value of information is computed by a deterministic scientific tool, not by an additional language model
every registered hypothesis carries an explicit pre-result prediction rule and an explicit falsification condition
a measurement that cannot separate any registered hypothesis scores zero discrimination, and that is a scientific result rather than a defect
weight sensitivity is reported as decision stability, never as model confidence
ties in the deterministic layer are reported as ties; the tool must not manufacture a preference it does not have
held-out result data are structurally removed before any payload is assembled
the mechanism question and the Agent framework are separate contributions and are reported separately

candidate_space.rationale: V4 deliberately reuses the byte-identical V3 lattice. Continuous-space optimization and any new wet-lab work are out of scope, so that the measured change between V3 and V4 is the decision object and the VOI layer, not the search space.

architecture.canonical_flow: planner(intent + failure mode) -> evidence/tool layer (including the deterministic VOI tool) -> proposer -> skeptic -> robustness adjudicator -> judge -> freeze
architecture.claim_boundary: V4.0.0 selects an experiment from pre-result evidence under an outcome-blind runtime. Its adjudication tests whether a registered hypothesis survives contact with the completed measurement. It is not a contemporaneous pre-experimental record and does not claim that the historical decision used this ranking.
architecture.name: PUR_NEW_VOI_GUIDED_EXPERIMENT_SELECTION_AGENT_V4
non_goals: adding a language model to compute value of information
adding Agent roles beyond planner, tools, proposer, skeptic, robustness adjudicator, judge and freeze
turning the study into a pure AI benchmark
weakening or replacing the rheological mechanism result
architecture.purpose: Outcome-blind scientific decision Agent that selects the next formulation x measurement EXPERIMENT by transparent value of information, rather than selecting a formulation candidate alone.

stages.role: identify the physical failure mode and the scientific question that the next experiment must answer, then request the evidence needed to judge experiments rather than formulations

execute read-only scientific tools, including the paper-derived state-aware rheology tool, external evidence retrieval, and the deterministic VOI tool that scores every formulation x measurement experiment card
propose the experiment with the highest scientific information value, stating the hypotheses it separates and what each possible outcome would establish
attack the proposed experiment on hypothesis coverage, confounding, interpretability of the primary observable, and whether the stated falsification criterion can actually be met by the measurement
adjudicate whether the proposed experiment survives the reported VOI weight sensitivity and the skeptic's strongest objection
commit to one experiment card, or abstain, and state the acceptance and falsification criteria that will adjudicate it
programmatically validate and freeze the experiment card with timestamps, model identifiers and cryptographic hashes of every input

architecture.supersedes_nothing: V4 is an independent architecture. configs/agent_v3.json, prompts/agent_v3_*.txt, src/pur_new/agent_v3.py and every frozen V3 run record remain unchanged and are not reinterpreted by V4.

planner.failure_mode: Viscosity growth during prolonged 120 C melt residence, with unresolved uncertainty about whether modifier effects suppress drift beyond reactive-core mass dilution.
planner.failure_mode_evidence: Original 120 C thermal-hold measurements show SI_15_60 of 9.51% for E1 versus 51.54% for E5, establishing substantial isothermal viscosity drift in the local design space.
planner.least_resolved_justification: The local data contain only one original thermal-hold run each for E1 and E5, both at 120 C with four time points from 15 to 90 minutes and no modifier-axis-resolved matched comparisons. By contrast, temperature response has six-point sweeps across 80-130 C with multiple E2 repeats, while the realized viscosity level has quantified E2 between-preparation spread.
measurement_requirements: Measure viscosity at 120 C at 15, 30, 45, and 60 minutes using at least two independent repeats and report SI_15_60.

Use a matched reactive mass fraction and explicitly recorded acrylic-like and minor tackifier-like composition axes so the result can distinguish reactive-core linear dilution, superlinear resin suppression, and tackifier-required dual-axis behavior.
Compare the measured drift with the preregistered linear-dilution prediction and retain the full time trajectory rather than only an endpoint.
planner.scientific_question: At matched reactive mass fraction and a matched 120 C hold window, does adding acrylic-like and/or minor tackifier-like modifier reduce viscosity drift substantially below the reactive-core linear-dilution prediction, and is entry into the low-drift regime dependent specifically on a nonzero minor tackifier axis?

hypotheses_not_separated: H-CORE versus H-DUAL if the measured drift is near the linear-dilution prediction

outcome_interpretation.if_acceptance_criterion_met: If SI_15_60 is below half the linear-dilution prediction, approximately 3.80% for the 20% acrylic composition, this supports H-RESIN, falsifies H-CORE, and falsifies H-DUAL because acrylic-only modification has entered the low-drift regime without a minor tackifier.
outcome_interpretation.if_falsification_criterion_met: If SI_15_60 remains at or above the linear-dilution prediction of approximately 7.61%, H-RESIN is falsified. The result is consistent with H-CORE and does not distinguish H-CORE from H-DUAL for an acrylic-only composition.
outcome_interpretation.if_intermediate: A drift between approximately 3.80% and 7.61% is below linear dilution but not below the preregistered half-linear threshold; it indicates possible suppression but is insufficient to support H-RESIN or falsify H-DUAL decisively.

ranked_alternatives.why_lower_value: The 15% acrylic plus 5% minor-tackifier composition lies inside both supported modifier regions and directly tests an active dual-axis intervention, but a low-drift result would not distinguish H-RESIN from H-DUAL because both predict suppression.

It provides the same acrylic-only attribution and hypothesis discrimination at the conservative 15% level, but the 15% external analogue is only directional and its formulation denominator is not fully verified, whereas 20% is directly commensurate and externally anchored.
A 5% minor-tackifier-only intervention tests the tackifier axis but does not directly test whether acrylic modification alone can suppress drift or separate H-RESIN from H-DUAL.

proposer.reasoning: S1C49 preserves the E2 reactive-core proportions, uses a directly supported 20% acrylic intervention within the supported 15-25% region, and applies the direct matched-window hold that measures the least-resolved failure coordinate. Its linear prediction is 9.51% x 0.80 = 7.61%, while H-RESIN predicts less than 3.80%. Unlike a dual-axis card, an acrylic-only low-drift result specifically falsifies the tackifier-required prediction, while a near-linear result falsifies superlinear resin suppression.

robustness_adjudication.change_from_proposal: Retain S1C49::M-HOLD-120, but require verification of acrylic identity and reactive functionality, recalculation of true NCO:OH stoichiometry and reactive mass fraction when necessary, and a prespecified aggregation rule for the two independent SI_15_60 repeats before interpreting the result mechanistically.
robustness_adjudication.departure_from_deterministic_ranking: Cannot be determined: the deterministic VOI ranking, tied top set, base_margin_to_first_strictly_lower, and recommendation_flip_boundary were withheld. No evidence establishes a departure from the ranking.
residual_decision_risk: The VOI decision stability cannot be assessed because the deterministic ranking and perturbation boundaries were withheld.
Even with verified stoichiometry, an acrylic-only result near the linear-dilution prediction leaves H-CORE versus H-DUAL entangled.
An intermediate drift result between the half-linear and linear thresholds may not support or falsify the registered hypotheses decisively.
The matched-window hold measures formulation-level rheological behavior and cannot establish the proposed molecular or encounter-frequency mechanism.
Two minimum repeats may be insufficient for robust threshold classification if between-repeat disagreement is substantial.
robustness_adjudication.skeptic_objection_reasoning: The strongest objection identifies a high-risk confound: the 20% acrylic modifier may not be chemically inert, so the 0.80 reactive mass fraction and 7.61% linear-dilution prediction may be invalid without verified functionality and recalculated NCO:OH stoichiometry. This requires verification before testing and prevents unique attribution to H-RESIN versus altered reactive stoichiometry if unresolved. It does not establish that another supplied experiment should replace the direct matched-window hold. The result must be interpreted as phenomenological drift behavior unless the modifier chemistry and stoichiometry are verified. Repeat aggregation should also be preregistered.
robustness_adjudication.weight_sensitivity_assessment: No weight perturbations can be assessed because the VOI score, tied top set, base_margin_to_first_strictly_lower, and recommendation_flip_boundary were withheld. Scientifically, M-HOLD-120 remains the appropriate measurement because it directly addresses the least-resolved isothermal drift coordinate.

skeptic.falsification_criterion_assessment: Yes. M-HOLD-120 directly measures SI_15_60 over the specified 15-60 minute window, and the 7.61% H-RESIN falsification threshold is separated from the 3.80% acceptance threshold by about 3.81 percentage points, exceeding the declared 2.0% discrimination resolution. Attainability is weakened near the threshold because the repeat-aggregation rule is unspecified.
leakage_findings: No outcome-derived formulation identity, wet-lab result, or post-result label is used; the proposal relies only on permitted original measurements and pre-result analogue evidence.
The rheological hold measurement cannot establish the specific H-RESIN molecular or encounter-frequency mechanism stated in the outcome interpretation.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: A result in the intermediate zone would not support H-RESIN or decisively falsify H-DUAL, so any binary mechanism conclusion would be unsupported.
objections.objection: The acrylic-only S1C49::M-HOLD-120 experiment cannot distinguish H-CORE from H-DUAL when SI_15_60 is near the linear-dilution prediction of 7.61%; the Proposer correctly declares this entanglement. It also has an intermediate zone from approximately 3.80% to 7.61% in which neither the H-RESIN acceptance threshold nor its stated falsification threshold is met.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: A drift change could be attributed to acrylic-mediated superlinear suppression when it actually results from altered stoichiometry or modifier reactivity, invalidating the H-RESIN versus H-CORE attribution.
objections.objection: S1C49 changes acrylic-like modifier content to 20% and reduces the reactive mass fraction to 0.80 simultaneously. The calculation 9.51% x 0.80 = 7.61% is interpretable as a dilution test only if the acrylic is chemically inert and contributes no NCO-reactive functionality. The supplied local-core note explicitly requires recalculation of NCO:OH if the modifier contributes reactive OH or another reactive group, but S1C49 does not specify verified functionality, identity, or a recalculated stoichiometry.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: The result cannot establish whether a minor tackifier is required except through the registered H-DUAL prediction; it cannot estimate an independent tackifier effect.
objections.objection: The intervention_family is acrylic_only, so the acrylic and minor-tackifier axes do not move together. This avoids the principal two-axis confounding problem; however, it also means the experiment provides no direct observation of the minor-tackifier axis.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: A threshold classification could depend on an unstated choice of mean, median, or individual-run value, weakening reproducibility near 3.80% or 7.61%.
objections.objection: The primary observable SI_15_60 is directly calculated from eta_15 and eta_60 in the M-HOLD-120 protocol, with no fit, extrapolation, or imputation. This attack surface is therefore largely survived. The remaining weakness is that the acceptance and falsification decisions use a point estimate from only the minimum two repeats, without a prespecified rule for aggregating repeats or handling between-repeat disagreement.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: The experiment can falsify H-RESIN in principle, but borderline outcomes may receive inconsistent classifications and may not meet the intended practical resolution.
objections.objection: The H-RESIN falsification criterion, SI_15_60 at or above 7.61%, is attainable because M-HOLD-120 directly measures the 15-60 minute change and the declared discrimination threshold is 2%, smaller than the approximately 3.81 percentage-point gap between the 7.61% linear prediction and the 3.80% half-linear threshold. However, the protocol does not state whether 7.61% is compared with a mean across the two repeats or whether repeat-level values must independently satisfy the criterion.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: The experiment would support a phenomenological superlinear suppression pattern, not the claimed concentration/encounter-frequency mechanism or any molecular explanation.
objections.objection: The proposal's outcome interpretation says that a low SI_15_60 supports the H-RESIN explanation involving lowered effective concentration and encounter frequency. M-HOLD-120 measures only viscosity-growth behavior; it cannot establish that specific physical mechanism. The registry limits adjudication to formulation-level rheological mechanisms and expressly excludes molecularly resolved pathways.

skeptic.recommended_change: Verify the acrylic identity and reactive functionality before the hold, recalculate the true NCO:OH ratio and reactive mass fraction if needed, and preregister how the two independent SI_15_60 repeats are aggregated. To resolve the admitted H-CORE versus H-DUAL entanglement, add a matched 5% minor-tackifier-only M-HOLD-120 composition with independently verified stoichiometry.
skeptic.strongest_objection: The S1C49 calculation assumes that the 20% acrylic-like modifier is chemically inert, yet the proposal does not verify modifier functionality or recalculate NCO:OH stoichiometry. If the modifier is reactive, the simultaneous change from reactive_mass_fraction 1.0 to 0.80 is not a pure dilution intervention, so SI_15_60 cannot uniquely discriminate H-RESIN from altered reactive stoichiometry or modifier reaction.

measurement_plan.protocol: Hold the melt at 120 C. Record viscosity at 15, 30, 45 and 60 min. Report the 15-60 min matched-window relative change. Run at least two independent repeats.

measurement_plan.name: repeatability / state-control experiment
measurement_plan.primary_observable: between-preparation spread of the realized viscosity-scale coordinate a_fr at matched temperature
measurement_plan.protocol: Prepare the same nominal composition three times under a controlled and fully recorded process history, then measure the 80-130 C sweep for each preparation.

measurement_plan.name: 80-130 C temperature sweep
measurement_plan.primary_observable: apparent temperature-response descriptor E_eta from ln(eta) versus 1/T
measurement_plan.protocol: Measure viscosity from 80 to 130 C in 10 C increments on a freshly prepared sample and regress ln(eta) against 1/T.
